Apple's "Surprise and Shine" event is scheduled for September 9, but the company has already surprised everyone by unveiling new products at the end of August this week. Here's why this rare move could signal major announcements at the September event.

August product launches hint at a September event already packed with new products

If you've been keeping a close eye on Apple, you'll start to notice a certain pattern in their product launch cycle throughout the year.

New products are typically released around March, followed by WWDC and software announcements in June, then a major event in September, with additional products often making appearances in October.

While it's not uncommon for smaller products to be announced via press releases at other points during the year, one thing is extremely rare: product launches at the end of August.

Over the past 10 years, Apple has only launched new hardware in August once. That product was the 2020 iMac, but it was unveiled on the 4th of that month.

Why are there no new product launches at the end of August? Because the September event is just around the corner, and new hardware is typically saved for that occasion.

In fact, the 2020 iMac isn't even a great example of breaking this convention. Due to COVID, Apple delayed that year's iPhone event from September to October.

However, despite plenty of evidence showing that products are never released in August, Apple still surprised everyone this week by unveiling new Mac mini and Mac Studio models two weeks before the September 9 event.

We know this isn't because Apple wanted to get the products into users' hands as quickly as possible. Why? Because these products won't start shipping until September 22.

The most obvious reason Apple unveiled these Macs early is that the "Surprise and Shine" event already has a ton of other products to announce.

Here's everything that might be unveiled at the September 9 event

Rumors suggest there should be at least five, and up to nine or more new products making their debut that day.

Products that are basically confirmed for the event include:

  • iPhone 18 Pro: Major camera upgrades, A20 Pro processor, new colors, updated Dynamic Island with more features
  • iPhone 18 Pro Max: Larger battery, potential exclusive camera features
  • iPhone Ultra: The first foldable model
  • Apple Watch Series 12: Upgraded S-series chip, more health features
  • Apple Watch Ultra 4: Brand new health sensors, refreshed design, more features

But there's also a strong chance of other products being unveiled, such as:

  • AirPods 5: New models with Active Noise Cancellation (ANC) and without ANC
  • All-new Apple TV 4K: Apple Intelligence support, Siri AI
  • HomePad: Smart home hub
  • HomePod mini 2: Upgraded chip, Siri AI support

If Apple overhauls the entire Home product line, we might also see the debut of the HomePod 3, as well as the rumored home security camera.

According to Mark Gurman, the chances of AirPods 5 launching are particularly high. He also hinted that new Home products would arrive in September.

Add all these products together, and September 9 is set to become one of the most content-packed Apple events in recent years. It also likely explains why Apple chose to move the Mac mini, Mac Studio, and M6 and M5 Ultra announcements up to August.

What do you expect Apple to announce on September 9? Let us know in the comments section.
